key_insight: Variational neural quantum state training can be reframed as a reinforcement learning trust-region problem, enabling a new optimizer that is both scalable and more stable than standard first-order or matrix-inversion-based methods.
engineering_relevance: PWO offers a practical way to train large autoregressive quantum wavefunction models with independent sampling, reduced numerical fragility, and better wall-clock convergence on hard spin-system benchmarks.
method: Reinterpret Born-distribution energy minimization as an advantage policy-gradient objective.
Apply proximal trust-region updates that clip amplitude probability ratios and phase increments separately.
Avoid explicit matrix inversion while reusing samples across multiple optimization steps.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on Ising and frustrated J1-J2 spin systems in one and two dimensions, where it improves stability and wall-clock convergence over Adam, minSR, and SPRING, and is also fine-tuned on a 1.5B-parameter RWKV-7 model.
watch_item: Trust-region clipping and sample reuse may improve efficiency, but performance can still depend on careful hyperparameter tuning and stable handling of amplitude-phase parameterization in large models.
paper_title: One More Time: Revisiting Neural Quantum States from a Reinforcement Learning Perspective
